text: Benchmark against neural frame extrapolation work (GFFE, PatchEX): borrow their disocclusion inpainting tricks
description: Research find (2026-11-23). GFFE (G-buffer-free frame extrapolation, ACM TOG 2024, Intel/UCSB; stereo follow-up 2025) extrapolates frames with no added latency and handles disocclusions with heuristics plus a small net. PatchEX (arXiv 2407.17501) splits extrapolation into inpainting and shadow sub-tasks, each a small net run per patch in parallel, aimed at VR. Amulet (arXiv 2608.10423): sparse layered scene representation for extrapolation. Task: read how they fill disocclusions (background-only fill from depth? learned infilling vectors like arXiv 2110.08805, which predicts where to copy from instead of colour) and test the most promising trick in train/ against nice-net on eval96 holes. Sources: https://sites.cs.ucsb.edu/~lingqi/publications/paper_gffe.pdf, https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17501, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.08805

status.comment: Research (abstracts): infilling vectors (Kanchana et al. WACV 2022) copy holes from a predicted offset; PatchEX: parallel patch inpainting. Both cheap variants tested, 500 its from nice-net, evaluate.py 64 x 96 mean L1: (1) background-biased push-pull (net.background 2, e62dfa7) vs nodrop: holes 0.1615 vs 0.1616, no effect. (2) infilling vectors (net.copy 6 px, f4a81cd, zero-initialised head) vs gate: holes 0.1634 vs 0.1624, all 0.0788 vs 0.0786; the head barely learned (|w| mean 0.009, offsets ~0.1-0.5 px), and the copy alone (max_change 0) made holes slightly worse (0.1848 vs 0.1837). No gain at this budget; options stay in train/ (default off).
